1484: Accustomed as he was to a Greek Christ and a German Mary, he was surprised to find in the place of the former a crucified Indian boy, whose traditional beard was no more than the sparse down that a beardless Indian might have grown, and to see that the Madonna was just a native woman with her head wrapped in her huipil and in her ears the big earrings the women of Zicxin wore.
She wore the shift and huipil of an Indian woman, and always round her neck a big rosary of coloured glass beads, ending in a metal crucifix.
